messages.subject: Pre-clustering step in Canopy
parts:
Hi Yuchao,

I noticed that in your paper you use a pre-clustering step on the somatic mutations in cases when many mutations are present.
Is that functionality implemented as part of Canopy, or do you suggest using a different tool (e.g. SciClone) for clustering mutations, followed by application of Canopy?

Thanks!
Vitor

I just uploaded our code for clustering onto this page: https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/tree/master/clustering . Cheers,

From: Yuchao Jiang <yj...@cornell.edu>

Subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Pre-clustering step in Canopy

 

Hi Victor,

 

Thanks for your interest in Canopy. SciClone will work (i.e., clustering 1D or 2D VAF into clusters and than fit each cluster as a mutation to Canopy with median depth of coverage of all mutations within the cluster) but we have codes that allow a bivariate Binomial pre-clustering step for MCMC. I'm not sure if the code is on GitHub but I will check tomorrow and push an update -- I've been traveling for job interviews and conferences and finally have a chance to fine tune Canopy, which is now of top priority. I will let you know once I test the codes again and push that onto GitHub.

 

Yuchao

messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Pre-clustering step in Canopy
parts:
Hi Victor,

When you get the column from R and X, it changes it to a vector instead of a matrix. This leads to the error that you saw. Canopy is primary for >=2 samples and for the clustering code I had we initialize the EM with k-means based on euclidean and correlation distance. Correlation won’t work for your case since it is only 1d. I modified the code though so you can run it through. Please update / reinstall Canopy from our GitHub page. The code I used is attached.

Also, I want to mention again that clustering is not the major contribution of Canopy but only a by-product. We don’t devote much time developing or maintaining it. Therefore, if you are working on benchmarking clustering algorithms, I think think it is fair to include Canopy. You can refer to Pyclone and SciClone which specifically tackle this issue.

All the best,
Yuchao
